Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 43, verses 1–5:

Makkiyyah (revealed in Makkah)

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1–3} This is an oath by the Qur'an concerning the Qur'an. He swears by "the Clear Book" (al-kitab al-mubin) without mentioning what it is related to, to indicate that it is clear (mubin) for everything that the servants need in matters of this world, their religion, and the Hereafter. {Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an} is the matter sworn to: that it was made in the most eloquent, clearest and most explicit of languages, and this is part of its clarity. He then mentions the wisdom behind this, saying: {so that you may understand}, its wording and its meanings, because they are made easy and close to minds.

{4} {And indeed it} — that is, this Book — {is with Us in the Mother of the Book} (lada-na) in the highest and most exalted rank, {exalted and full of wisdom}; that is, exalted in its worth, its nobility and its station, and full of wisdom in what it contains of commands, prohibitions and reports. There is therefore in it no ruling that contradicts wisdom, justice and balance.

{5} Then He informs that His wisdom and His grace require that He not leave His servants neglected, without sending them a Messenger or sending down to them a Book, even if they are wasteful and wrongdoers. So He says: {Shall We then withhold the Reminder from you, turning away from you, because you are a people who transgress?} — that is, shall We turn away from you and cease sending down the Reminder to you, withholding it from you because of your aversion and your failure to submit [to it]? Rather, We send down the Book to you and make clear to you in it everything. So if you believe in it and are guided, it is from your success (tawfiq); otherwise, the proof is established against you, and you were upon clear evidence of your affair.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on verses 6–8:

{6–8} He says, exalted is He: This is Our way with creation, that We do not leave them neglected. How many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples, who commanded them to worship Allah alone, with no partner. Denial has never ceased to exist among the nations. "And there never came to them a prophet but that they used to mock him," rejecting what he brought and being arrogant toward the truth. "Then We destroyed those who were stronger than these in might" — that is, in power, deeds, and traces left upon the earth. "And the example of the former peoples has passed on" — that is, their likenesses and their histories have passed away, and We have made clear to you from them what contains a lesson and a deterrent from denial and rejection.

{9} God, exalted is He, informs that if you were to ask the polytheists, ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth?﴾, they would surely say, ﴿God﴾, alone, with no partner for Him. ﴿The Mighty﴾: the One before whose might all creatures submit. ﴿The Knowing﴾: of the outward and inward aspects of matters, and of their beginnings and their ends. If they acknowledge this, then how do they ascribe offspring, consorts and partners to Him? And how do they associate with Him those who create nothing, provide nothing, cause no death and give no life?

{10} Then He mentions, among the proofs of His complete blessing and power, the earth that He spread out and made a resting place for His servants, where they can settle and do everything they wish. ﴿And He has made for you therein roads﴾: that is, He made passages between the connected chains of mountains through which you pass to the regions beyond them. ﴿That you may be guided﴾: in traveling the paths without going astray, and that you may also be guided in reflecting upon and contemplating this.

{11} ﴿And who sends down water from the sky in measure﴾: neither more nor less, and in an amount that meets the need. It is not so little as to be of no benefit, nor so much as to harm the servants and the lands. Rather, He gives relief to the servants with it and rescues the lands from hardship. For this reason He says: ﴿So We revive thereby a dead land﴾: that is, We give it life after its death. ﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾: just as He revives the dead, lifeless earth with water, so He will revive you after you have passed through the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection), so that He may recompense you for your deeds.

{12} ﴿And who created all the pairs﴾: that is, all the kinds: whatever the earth produces, and of themselves, and of what they do not know; such as night and day, heat and cold, male and female, and other things. ﴿And made for you of the ships and cattle that you ride﴾: that is, the sea vessels, sailing and steam-powered, that you ride.

{13} ﴿That you may sit upon their backs﴾: this includes the backs of ships and of livestock; that is, that you may settle upon them. ﴿Then remember the favor of your Lord when you are seated upon them﴾: by acknowledging the blessing to the One who subjected them to you, and by praising Him, exalted is He, for it. Among them: a son is a part of his father, while Allah is distinct from His creation and different from them in His attributes and the qualities of His majesty, and a son is a part of his father. So it is impossible that Allah should have a son.

{16} Among them: they claim that the angels are daughters of Allah. It is well known that daughters are the inferior of the two sexes. How could Allah have daughters, and choose for Himself sons while preferring them with daughters?! In that case, they would be better than Allah! Exalted is Allah far above that, a great exaltation!

{17} Among them: the category they attributed to Allah, namely daughters, is the inferior and most detested of the two categories by them. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 43, verses 26–32:

{26} He, exalted is He, informs us about the creed (millah) of Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, to whom both the People of the Book and the polytheists trace their lineage, and each of them claims to be upon his way. So He informs us of his religion, which he bequeathed to his descendants, saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim said to his father and his people﴾, those who took besides Allah gods which they worship and draw near to: ﴿Indeed, I am free from what you worship﴾; that is, I am one who hates it, avoids it, and is hostile to its adherents.

{27} ﴿Except He who created me﴾; for indeed I take Him as my ally ( atawallahu) and hope that He will guide me to knowledge of the truth and to acting upon the truth. Just as He created me and ordered my affairs in what sets right my body and my worldly life, so He will guide me to what sets right my religion and my hereafter.

{28} ﴿And He made it﴾; that is, this praiseworthy trait, which is the mother of all good qualities and its foundation, namely sincerely devoting worship to Allah alone and disavowing the worship of anything other than Him, ﴿a word that remains in his descendants﴾; that is, among his offspring, ﴿that they may return﴾ to it. [This is] because of its fame from him and his charge to his descendants, and the charge of some of his sons, such as Ishaq and Ya'qub, to others, as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And who would turn away from the creed of Ibrahim except one who makes a fool of himself...﴾ to the end of the verses.

{29} This word continued to exist among his descendants, peace be upon him, until affluence and tyranny entered them. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 43, verses 84–89:

{84} Allah, the Exalted, informs that He alone is the One worthy of worship (al-ma'luh al-ma'bud) in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He alone has exclusive knowledge of the unseen, which none of creation has been informed of, neither a sent prophet nor a near angel. Hence He said: ﴿And with Him is knowledge of the Hour﴾. He placed the adverbial phrase first to indicate restriction; that is, none knows when the Hour will come except Him. And part of the completeness of His dominion and vastness is that He is the owner of this world and the Hereafter. Hence He said: ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾; that is, in the Hereafter, when He will judge between you with His just judgment.

{86} And part of the completeness of His dominion is that none of His creation possesses any part of the command, and no one may approach Him for intercession except by His permission. ﴿And those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession﴾; that is, everyone invoked besides Allah, whether prophets, angels or others, does not possess intercession, and they do not intercede except by Allah's permission, and they intercede only for those whom He approves. Hence He said: ﴿except one who testifies to the truth﴾; that is, one who speaks with his tongue while affirming in his heart, knowing what he testifies to. It is required that his testimony be to the truth, which is testifying to Allah's oneness (tawhid al-uluhiyyah, the affirmation of His sole right to worship) and to His messengers' prophethood and messengership, and to the soundness of what they brought of the foundations of religion, its branches, its realities and its laws. These are the ones for whom the intercession of intercessors will benefit, and these are the ones who are saved from Allah's punishment and attain His reward.

{87} Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾; that is, if you asked the polytheists about the oneness of Lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah, the affirmation of Allah's sole lordship and creation) and who is the Creator, they would acknowledge that it is Allah alone, without partner. ﴿Then how are they deluded?﴾; that is, how are they turned away from worshipping Allah and devoting worship to Him alone? Their affirmation of the oneness of Lordship obligates them to affirm the oneness of divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah), and this is among the greatest proofs of the falsehood of shirk (association of partners with Allah).

{88} ﴿And [He has knowledge of] his saying, "My Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe"﴾. This is joined to His saying: ﴿And with Him is knowledge of the Hour﴾; that is, and with Him is knowledge of his statement, namely the Messenger (ﷺ) complaining to his Lord of his people's denial, grieving over that and lamenting their lack of faith. Allah, the Exalted, knows this condition, and is able to hasten their punishment, but He, the Exalted, is forbearing, He gives respite to the servants and waits patiently with them, perhaps they will repent and return.

{89} For this reason He said: ﴿So overlook [their offense] and say, "Peace"﴾; that is, overlook whatever harm comes to you from them, in speech or in action, pardon them, and let there come from you toward them only the peace with which people of intellect and insight meet the ignorant. As Allah said about His righteous servants: ﴿And when the ignorant address them﴾; that is, with address befitting their ignorance, ﴿they say, "Peace."﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) complied with his Lord's command, and received the harm that came to him from his people and others with pardon and forgiveness, and he did not respond to them, peace be upon him, except with kindness toward them and gentle speech. So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon the one whom Allah singled out with the great character by which he surpassed the people of the earth and the heavens, and through which he rose higher than the stars of Orion. And His saying: ﴿But they will soon know﴾; that is, the consequence of their sins and the outcome of their crimes.

Here ends the tafsir of Surat al-Zukhruf. All praise and grace belong to Allah.
